newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Canada's Bre-X refuses comment in Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Bre-X refuses comment in Indonesia.

text.p: The Jakarta office of the Canadian gold exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd refused comment on Thursday on the state of an application for a Contract of Work covering a huge gold find in Indonesia's East Kalimantan.
"I can't answer anything," an official said, referring all queries to the company's office in Toronto.
Bre-X has applied for a sixth generation contract of work (COW) at its Busang property covering Busang II and III.
But an Indonesian partner, PT Krueng Gasui with a 10 percent stake in Busang I, has also claimed a 10-percent interest in Busang II and III.
Bre-X has calculated the gold resource in Busang I at about three million ounces. But the overall estimate for the property is at least 47 million ounces, with the richest deposit in Busang II.
Bre-X has said that its Indonesian legal adviser had told it the partner's claims to a 10-percent share of Busang II and III were without merit.

Indonesias's director of mines, Kuntoro Mangkusubroto, told a mining seminar in Tokyo on October 3 that approval was expected by the end of the month for 70 applications from foreign firms and joint ventures for sixth generation COWs to explore and develop mineral deposits.
Bre-X stock has traded heavily on the Toronto Stock Exchange in recent days. It was down 25 cents to $25.05 on Wednesday.
